title: Semi-concavity and semidefinite characteristics
source_hypothesis: Proper scalar classical operator of real order, condition P, compact regular persistent one-dimensional characteristic interval with nonzero semidefinite quadratic endpoints; explicit admissible quotient clock.
completed_component_scope: A decreasing regularity profile obeys a stronger comparison rule than an increasing one. This asymmetry is the useful notion of semi-concavity in the principal-type propagation problem. We first prove its exact shape classification and endpoint rules. We then prove propagation on the entire semidefinite characteristic stratum, with the parameter construction justified separately from the analytic estimate.
reviewed_arguments: Both directions of the extended-valued quasi-concavity and semi-concavity classification are proved. Included endpoints have separate sharp lower-cap conditions, avoiding a false interior turning rule at a closed endpoint.

Local semi-concavity implies global semi-concavity by an attained lower-semicontinuous minimum against a strictly convex quadratic perturbation. No false local-to-global claim about quasi-concavity is used.

Condition P transports the nonpositive semidefinite orientation through the ordinary full-interval tube. The actual zero-Hessian fibers and compact quotient are identified without assuming proportionality.

Radial curves have constant conic indices. Every nonradial collapsed fiber has an embedded cosphere projection and a homogeneous tube with nonzero-Hessian endpoints; the earlier whole-fiber proof uses only the zero stratum and these nonzero endpoints.
Nonnegative semidefinite division gives a favorable one-sign tube or a remainder flat on the full central fiber. Only the latter case uses exact proportionality of the transported quadratic forms.

The favorable set is open and saturated by entire quotient fibers. A smooth compact correction of the transported-form norm produces a global clock with precisely the zero-Hessian fibers. The reparametrization factor is explicit: b(t) dt equals a positive constant times h(theta) dtheta on every flat-remainder tube.

The rank-changing one-sign example disproves blanket Hessian proportionality and unique affine structure. It admits two non-affinely related valid clocks. That source defect is retained and resolved by the explicit admissible-clock theorem, not certified as a true assertion.

Whole-fiber graph equivalence and elliptic order reduction give the exact all-real source shift m minus one. The corrected theorem covers every interval with the original semidefinite endpoint hypothesis.
One-sign propagation proves decreasing-affine comparison for any increasing clock, with a uniform strict source and incoming margin on each compact fiber.

Three mollified distance cutoffs have full S(1-epsilon,epsilon) derivative bounds and exact strict plateaus. The constants 256, 16 and 1 account for overlapping dyadic scales and normalized-distance distortion.

Time-independent full-frequency ordinary cutoffs preserve the sign on the outer plateau. Proper localization and arbitrarily deep finite symbol expansions justify all smaller-cone mapping assertions on the actual distribution.

The complete complex-cutoff theorem applies up to epsilon equals one quarter with weak input L minus one eighth and exactly the measured forcing and incoming data. The weighted-composition error gives actual H to the L membership of both favorable pieces.

The full spacetime commutator includes minus f_t times the tau derivative of the cutoff. Its factorization has orders epsilon and 3 epsilon minus one, including all mixed, exotic and lower-order remainders.

Every derivative of the remainder is flat on the closed positive set. Normalized-distance estimates and arbitrarily deep finite product remainders prove the complete operator error is smoothing on the actual input.

The modified operator has the exact factorized principal symbol and condition P. The preceding complete descent theorem applies with the actual affine clock, giving the L-minus-epsilon index bound and then its all-epsilon limit.
Twenty-four exact algebraic checks, 370 parsed formulas, 37 displays, twenty inspected lesson captures, three complete solutions and an original reproducible figure support the receiving review.
